new_claim: For every fixed finite-state row-centered graphon kernel W, cycle pressure still forces n theta^2 ||T_W||_op^2<=1+o(1). If the global replica energy obeys the entropy domination ratio R=E_ent(W,mu)/||T_W||_op^2 and rho^2 R<1, the entire noisy likelihood ratio is uniformly bounded in L2, so no test can strongly distinguish. The rank-one model has R=1 exactly. A new finite-type lemma proves sup_n E exp(gamma n D(hat_nu||nu))<infinity for every gamma<1, so the global inequality Q_K(pi)<=2 E_ent D(pi||nu) closes the second moment whenever rho^2 E_ent/||T_W||_op^2<1. For the Potts obstruction, graph moments are nowhere-zero Z_q-flow counts. Suppressing degree-2 paths in connected bridgeless graphs shows all positive-excess contributions through degree D total O_q(D^10/n), while cycle contributions sum geometrically for alpha<1; hence LDA stays bounded. After noise, a union bound over near-balanced labelings controls the null maximum score, whereas the true latent labeling has mean sqrt(c)(q-1)n^{3/2}/2, giving strong exhaustive distinction when c=alpha rho^2>4 log q/(q-1).
strictness_example: For W_q(a,b)=q 1_{a=b}-1 with uniform q-state labels, the one-replica operator has spectral radius one, but the diagonal replica type has energy q-1 and entropy log q, so E_ent>=(q-1)/(2 log q)>1 for q>=4. This explicitly separates the local cycle/Hessian threshold from the global overlap-pressure threshold.
mao_boundary: Mao remains a stronger polynomial-time counterexample: his LDA is exactly zero through Theta((log n)^{r-1}) and a polynomial-time rank test survives every fixed positive noise rate. The Potts obstruction here only gives bounded (not zero) polylog-degree LDA and an exponential-time strong test for sufficiently weak fixed noise. Its role is to prove that an unrestricted all-test strengthening is the wrong target for general finite-state graphons, not to weaken Mao's boundary or solve the source problem.
exact_gap: The source asks for conditions under which bounded polylog-degree LDA controls higher-degree polynomial distinguishers. The present finite-state theorem controls all tests only under global entropy-overlap domination, while the Potts example shows that natural finite-state models can have a nonlocal overlap state outside that regime. What remains is a degree-sensitive theorem proving that low-degree or moderately higher-degree polynomials cannot exploit such nonlocal overlap states even when exhaustive search can.
